explanationCorrect: S3 One Zone-IA stores infrequently accessed data in a single AZ at lower cost than Standard-IA while keeping millisecond retrieval, suitable when the data can be recreated if the AZ is lost.
explanationIncorrect: S3 Standard costs more and is meant for frequent access. Glacier Deep Archive is cheaper but has long retrieval times, so it is not instantly retrievable. Provisioned IOPS EBS is costly high-performance block storage, not a low-cost class for infrequent object access.

stem: To make a web tier resilient to the failure of an entire Availability Zone, what should the architecture do?

options.text: Run instances across multiple Availability Zones behind a load balancer with an Auto Scaling group
Run all instances in a single AZ with a larger instance type
Use one instance with frequent snapshots
Place all instances in one subnet in one AZ

explanationCorrect: Distributing instances across multiple AZs behind a load balancer, managed by an Auto Scaling group, lets the application survive the loss of an entire AZ.
explanationIncorrect: A single larger instance in one AZ still fails entirely if that AZ goes down. One instance with snapshots offers recovery but not continuous availability during a failure. Placing everything in one subnet in one AZ concentrates risk, so multi-AZ behind a load balancer is the resilient design.

stem: An application needs a relational database that automatically fails over to a standby with minimal downtime if the primary fails. Which RDS feature provides this?

options.text: RDS Multi-AZ deployment with a synchronous standby
A single-AZ RDS instance with automated backups
A read replica in the same AZ
Storing the database on an instance store volume

explanationCorrect: RDS Multi-AZ maintains a synchronous standby in another AZ and automatically fails over to it if the primary becomes unavailable, minimizing downtime.
explanationIncorrect: A single-AZ instance with backups can be restored but does not fail over automatically. A read replica is for scaling reads and is asynchronous, not an automatic HA failover target by default. Instance store is ephemeral and unsuitable for a durable database, so Multi-AZ is the correct feature.

stem: To decouple a producer service from a slower consumer so that traffic spikes do not overwhelm the consumer, which service should sit between them?
explanationCorrect: An SQS queue buffers messages between producer and consumer, letting the consumer process at its own pace and absorbing spikes for a more resilient, decoupled design.
explanationIncorrect: CloudFront caches content at the edge and does not buffer work between services. Direct Connect is a dedicated network link, not a decoupling buffer. Route 53 is DNS, so an SQS queue is the correct decoupling mechanism.

stem: Which Route 53 routing policy improves resilience by directing traffic away from an endpoint that fails its health check?

options.text: Simple routing with a single record
Weighted routing with fixed weights and no health checks
Geolocation routing based only on country

explanationCorrect: Failover routing uses health checks to send traffic to a primary endpoint and automatically shift to a standby when the primary is unhealthy.
explanationIncorrect: Simple routing returns one record with no health-based failover. Weighted routing without health checks keeps sending a share of traffic to an unhealthy endpoint. Geolocation routing selects by user location, not by endpoint health, so failover routing is the resilient choice.

stem: A stateful application stores session data on individual instances, causing user sessions to break when Auto Scaling replaces an instance. What is the best fix?

options.text: Externalize session state to a shared store such as Amazon ElastiCache or DynamoDB
Disable Auto Scaling so instances never change
Use larger instances so they fail less often
Store sessions on instance store volumes

explanationCorrect: Moving session state to a shared external store like ElastiCache or DynamoDB makes instances stateless, so replacing them does not break user sessions.
explanationIncorrect: Disabling Auto Scaling sacrifices elasticity and resilience to work around the design flaw. Larger instances still fail eventually and lose local sessions. Instance store is ephemeral and lost on instance termination, so externalizing session state is the correct fix.

stem: Which S3 capability protects against accidental deletion or overwrite by keeping multiple variants of an object?
explanationCorrect: S3 Versioning retains previous versions of an object, so an accidental delete or overwrite can be recovered by restoring an earlier version.
explanationIncorrect: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads over long distances and does not protect against deletion. Requester Pays shifts data transfer costs to the requester. Static website hosting serves content, so Versioning is the feature that guards against accidental changes.

stem: To recover a multi-tier application in another Region after a disaster while keeping ongoing costs low and accepting some recovery time, which DR strategy fits?

options.text: Pilot light, keeping core components minimally running and scaling up on failover
Backup and restore only, with no pre-provisioned core
No DR plan, relying on a single Region

explanationCorrect: Pilot light keeps critical core components running minimally in the recovery Region so you can scale them up quickly on failover, balancing cost against recovery time.
explanationIncorrect: Active-active offers the fastest recovery but at the highest ongoing cost, more than the scenario wants. Backup and restore is cheapest but slower to recover than pilot light and pre-provisions no core. No DR plan leaves the application exposed, so pilot light matches the cost-versus-recovery balance.

stem: An Auto Scaling group should replace instances that are running but no longer serving traffic correctly. Which health check type detects this application-level failure?

options.text: ELB health checks, so unhealthy targets per the load balancer are replaced

explanationCorrect: Configuring the Auto Scaling group to use ELB health checks lets it consider an instance unhealthy when the load balancer's application-level check fails, then replace it.
explanationIncorrect: EC2 status checks only detect infrastructure or system issues, not an app that is up but returning errors. Billing alarms track spend, not instance health. S3 event notifications fire on object changes, so ELB health checks are needed to catch application-level failures.

stem: Which storage service provides a shared file system that can be mounted concurrently by many EC2 instances across multiple AZs?
explanationCorrect: Amazon EFS is a managed elastic NFS file system that many instances across multiple AZs can mount concurrently, supporting shared, resilient access.
explanationIncorrect: A standard EBS volume attaches to a single instance in one AZ. Instance store is ephemeral and local to one instance. Glacier is archival object storage, not a mountable file system, so EFS is the shared multi-AZ file system.

stem: A read-heavy relational workload is straining the primary database. Which approach best scales read throughput?

options.text: Add read replicas and route read queries to them
Increase the primary's storage size only

explanationCorrect: Read replicas offload read traffic from the primary, scaling read throughput horizontally for read-heavy workloads.
explanationIncorrect: Adding storage does not increase query throughput for reads. Multi-AZ provides high availability, not read scaling, since the standby does not serve reads. More frequent snapshots aid backup but do not scale reads, so read replicas are the right approach.

stem: A DynamoDB table experiences hot partitions and throttling because many requests target the same partition key. What design change most improves performance?

options.text: Choose a high-cardinality partition key that distributes requests evenly
Reduce the number of items in the table
Switch the table to a single partition key value
Add more global secondary indexes with the same key

explanationCorrect: Selecting a partition key with high cardinality spreads requests across many partitions, avoiding hot partitions and throttling.
explanationIncorrect: Reducing item count does not fix an uneven access pattern. Forcing a single partition key value concentrates all traffic onto one partition, worsening the problem. Adding indexes on the same skewed key repeats the hot-partition issue, so a high-cardinality key is the correct fix.

stem: To reduce database load for frequently read, rarely changing data, which service adds an in-memory caching layer?
explanationCorrect: Amazon ElastiCache provides managed in-memory caches (Redis or Memcached) that serve frequently accessed data quickly and offload the database.
explanationIncorrect: Glacier is archival storage with retrieval delays, the opposite of a fast cache. Snowball transfers bulk data physically. Athena runs SQL queries over S3 data and is not a caching layer, so ElastiCache is the correct in-memory cache.

stem: Global users report slow load times for static assets served from a single Region. Which service reduces latency by serving content from edge locations?
explanationCorrect: CloudFront caches content at edge locations worldwide, so users are served from a nearby edge, reducing latency for static assets.
explanationIncorrect: EBS is block storage for a single instance and does not distribute content globally. AWS Config tracks configuration compliance. SQS is a message queue, so CloudFront is the service that improves global content delivery performance.

stem: An application needs very low-latency, high-throughput block storage for a demanding transactional database on EC2. Which EBS volume type is most appropriate?
explanationCorrect: Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes deliver consistent, high IOPS and low latency, making them suited to demanding transactional databases.
explanationIncorrect: Cold HDD is optimized for infrequently accessed, throughput-oriented data at low cost, not low-latency transactions. Throughput Optimized HDD targets large sequential workloads, not high random IOPS. Magnetic is a legacy low-performance option, so Provisioned IOPS SSD is the right choice.

stem: Which approach lets a fleet of EC2 instances automatically add capacity as CPU utilization rises and remove it as demand drops?

options.text: An Auto Scaling group with a target tracking scaling policy
Vertical scaling by rebooting into a bigger type each time

explanationCorrect: An Auto Scaling group with a target tracking policy automatically adjusts capacity to keep a metric like CPU utilization near a target, scaling out and in with demand.
explanationIncorrect: Manually launching instances does not respond automatically and lags demand. A fixed-size fleet cannot adapt to load changes. Repeatedly rebooting into bigger types is disruptive vertical scaling that does not elastically track demand, so a target tracking Auto Scaling policy is correct.

stem: A data analytics team needs to run complex SQL queries over petabytes of structured data in a data warehouse. Which service is purpose-built for this?
explanationCorrect: Amazon Redshift is a managed, columnar data warehouse optimized for complex analytical SQL queries over very large structured datasets.
explanationIncorrect: DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value store, not a warehouse for complex analytical joins at petabyte scale. ElastiCache is an in-memory cache. SQS is a message queue, so Redshift is the data-warehouse service.

stem: A read-heavy application on DynamoDB needs microsecond read latency for repeated hot keys. Which fully managed cache fits DynamoDB specifically?
explanationCorrect: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed in-memory cache purpose-built for DynamoDB, delivering microsecond read latency for hot items.
explanationIncorrect: CloudFront caches web content at edges, not DynamoDB item reads. RDS Proxy pools connections for relational databases, not DynamoDB. Global Accelerator optimizes network paths, not database item caching, so DAX is the DynamoDB-specific cache.

stem: To process a large volume of independent tasks in parallel without managing servers, which pairing is a good serverless fit?

options.text: Amazon SQS triggering AWS Lambda functions that scale with the queue
A single EC2 instance polling a database in a loop
Amazon CloudFront with an origin group

explanationCorrect: SQS decouples and buffers tasks while Lambda scales out to process messages in parallel, giving a serverless, elastic processing pipeline.
explanationIncorrect: A single EC2 instance polling in a loop does not scale in parallel and requires server management. Route 53 weighted records handle DNS traffic distribution, not task processing. CloudFront origin groups provide failover for content delivery, so SQS with Lambda is the serverless parallel-processing fit.

stem: An EC2 application needs to read from an S3 bucket. What is the most secure way to grant this access?

options.text: Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance with a policy allowing the needed S3 actions
Embed an IAM user's access keys in the application code
Store root credentials on the instance

explanationCorrect: Attaching an IAM role to the instance provides temporary, automatically rotated credentials scoped to the needed S3 actions, with no long-lived keys to manage.
explanationIncorrect: Embedding static access keys in code risks leaking long-lived credentials. Making the bucket public exposes data far beyond the application. Storing root credentials on the instance is extremely dangerous, so an IAM role is the secure approach.

stem: A database in a private subnet must never be reachable from the internet but needs to download OS patches. Which design meets both needs?

options.text: Place it in a private subnet and route outbound traffic through a NAT gateway in a public subnet
Place it in a public subnet with an Elastic IP
Attach an internet gateway route directly to the database instance

explanationCorrect: A private subnet keeps the database unreachable from the internet, while a NAT gateway in a public subnet lets it make outbound connections for patches without accepting inbound traffic.
explanationIncorrect: A public subnet with an Elastic IP exposes the database to the internet. Routing an internet gateway directly to the instance makes it publicly reachable. Opening SSH to the world is a severe exposure, so a private subnet with a NAT gateway satisfies both requirements.

stem: Which mechanism controls inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level acting as a stateful virtual firewall?
explanationCorrect: Security groups are stateful virtual firewalls attached to instances (via their network interfaces) that control allowed inbound and outbound traffic.
explanationIncorrect: IAM policies govern API permissions, not network packet flow. S3 bucket policies control access to bucket objects, not instance traffic. Route 53 records handle DNS resolution, so security groups are the instance-level stateful firewall.

stem: A subnet needs an additional stateless layer of network filtering that applies to all traffic entering and leaving the subnet. Which construct provides this?
explanationCorrect: Network ACLs are stateless subnet-level filters that evaluate rules on all traffic entering and leaving a subnet, complementing security groups.
explanationIncorrect: IAM roles grant API permissions, not subnet packet filtering. KMS keys handle encryption, not network rules. CloudWatch alarms trigger on metrics, so NACLs are the stateless subnet-level filtering construct.

stem: Data stored in S3 must be encrypted at rest with keys whose usage is auditable and controlled by the organization. Which option meets this?

options.text: Server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)
No encryption, relying on bucket privacy

explanationCorrect: SSE-KMS encrypts objects at rest using KMS keys with fine-grained key policies and CloudTrail-audited usage, meeting controlled and auditable encryption requirements.
explanationIncorrect: Relying only on bucket privacy leaves data unencrypted at rest. Renaming files is not encryption and provides no protection. Disabling versioning is unrelated to encryption, so SSE-KMS is the correct choice for auditable, controlled encryption.

stem: An application must retrieve database credentials at runtime with automatic rotation. Which service is designed for this?
explanationCorrect: AWS Secrets Manager securely stores credentials, provides them to applications at runtime, and can automatically rotate them on a schedule.
explanationIncorrect: Storing credentials in S3 lacks built-in rotation and secret-specific controls. CloudTrail logs API activity but does not manage secrets. SNS delivers notifications, so Secrets Manager is the service built for credential storage and rotation.

stem: To let users sign in to a web and mobile app and obtain temporary AWS access scoped to their identity, which service provides user pools and identity federation?
explanationCorrect: Amazon Cognito provides user pools for sign-up and sign-in and identity pools that grant temporary, scoped AWS credentials, including federation with external identity providers.
explanationIncorrect: AWS Config tracks resource configuration, not user authentication. Inspector assesses vulnerabilities. AWS Glue is an ETL service, so Cognito is the service for app user authentication and federation.

stem: You want EC2 instances in a private subnet to reach Amazon S3 without traversing the public internet or a NAT gateway. Which feature enables this?

options.text: A VPC gateway endpoint for S3
An internet gateway attached to the private subnet
A public Elastic IP on each instance

explanationCorrect: A VPC gateway endpoint for S3 provides private connectivity to S3 through route table entries, keeping traffic on the AWS network without a NAT gateway or internet access.
explanationIncorrect: An internet gateway would route traffic over the public internet, defeating the goal. Public Elastic IPs expose instances rather than keeping traffic private. A private hosted zone resolves DNS names but does not create private S3 connectivity, so a gateway endpoint is the correct feature.

stem: Which practice reduces the blast radius if a single set of IAM permissions is compromised?

options.text: Grant least-privilege permissions scoped to specific actions and resources
Use one shared IAM user for everyone
Disable CloudTrail to reduce logging overhead

explanationCorrect: Scoping permissions to only the specific actions and resources needed limits what a compromised credential can do, shrinking the blast radius.
explanationIncorrect: Attaching AdministratorAccess broadly maximizes the damage from any compromise. A shared IAM user removes accountability and widens exposure. Disabling CloudTrail removes the audit trail you need for detection, so least-privilege scoping is the correct practice.

stem: Infrequently accessed data must remain retrievable within milliseconds but should cost less than S3 Standard. Which storage class fits?
explanationCorrect: S3 Standard-IA offers millisecond retrieval at a lower storage price than Standard, suited to infrequently accessed but still readily available data.
explanationIncorrect: Glacier Deep Archive is far cheaper but has retrieval times of hours, not milliseconds. S3 Standard costs more and is meant for frequent access. Instance store is ephemeral local disk, not durable object storage, so Standard-IA matches the requirements.

stem: A workload has unpredictable access patterns and you do not want to manage lifecycle transitions manually while still optimizing storage cost. Which S3 option helps?

options.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which moves objects between tiers automatically based on access
S3 Standard with no lifecycle rules
Glacier Deep Archive for all objects regardless of access

explanationCorrect: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on usage, optimizing cost for unpredictable patterns without manual lifecycle management.
explanationIncorrect: Standard with no rules keeps everything at the higher price regardless of access. Manual weekly deletion is error prone and not a tiering strategy. Forcing everything into Deep Archive would break millisecond access needs, so Intelligent-Tiering fits unpredictable access.

stem: A steady-state production workload runs 24/7 for at least a year. Which EC2 pricing model minimizes cost while keeping capacity reserved?

options.text: Reserved Instances or a Compute Savings Plan with a one- or three-year commitment
Spot Instances for the steady workload

explanationCorrect: For predictable, always-on workloads, a Reserved Instance or Compute Savings Plan commitment provides significant discounts over On-Demand while ensuring capacity.
explanationIncorrect: On-Demand is the most expensive option for continuous long-running use. Spot can be reclaimed at any time, unsuitable for steady production needs. Dedicated Hosts add premium cost for physical isolation not required here, so a Reserved or Savings Plan commitment is most cost effective.

stem: A fault-tolerant batch processing job runs at flexible times and can restart if interrupted. Which purchasing option minimizes its cost?
explanationCorrect: Spot Instances offer the deepest discounts for interruption-tolerant, flexible workloads like fault-tolerant batch jobs.
explanationIncorrect: On-Demand costs more and is unnecessary for interruptible work. Reserved Instances require a commitment better suited to steady workloads, not flexible batch runs. Dedicated Hosts are premium-priced for isolation, so Spot Instances minimize cost here.

stem: A sporadically used internal API receives a few thousand requests per day with long idle periods. Which architecture is most cost-effective?

options.text: API Gateway with AWS Lambda, paying only per request and execution time
A fleet of always-on EC2 instances behind a load balancer
A large Reserved Instance running continuously

explanationCorrect: A serverless API Gateway and Lambda design charges only for actual requests and compute time, so long idle periods incur little cost, ideal for sporadic traffic.
explanationIncorrect: Always-on EC2 instances incur cost during the long idle periods regardless of traffic. A continuously running Reserved Instance commits to capacity that mostly sits idle. A provisioned Redshift cluster is an analytics warehouse, unnecessary and costly here, so serverless is the cost-effective choice.

stem: To automatically move older S3 objects to cheaper storage classes and eventually expire them, what should you configure?
explanationCorrect: S3 Lifecycle rules automatically transition objects to lower-cost classes over time and can expire them on a schedule, optimizing storage cost.
explanationIncorrect: Cross-Region Replication copies objects to another Region and does not reduce storage cost. CloudFront caches content for delivery, not lifecycle management. An SQS queue moves messages, so Lifecycle rules are the correct cost-optimization feature.

stem: Which practice helps avoid paying for idle over-provisioned EC2 capacity?

options.text: Right-sizing instances based on utilization metrics and using Auto Scaling
Always choosing the largest instance type to be safe
Running fixed capacity sized for peak at all times

explanationCorrect: Right-sizing based on actual utilization and letting Auto Scaling match capacity to demand avoids paying for idle, over-provisioned resources.
explanationIncorrect: Always choosing the largest type wastes money on unused capacity. Sizing fixed capacity for peak means paying for peak resources during low demand. Disabling monitoring removes the very data needed to optimize and does not save meaningfully, so right-sizing with Auto Scaling is correct.

stem: Large volumes of data transferred out from EC2 to the internet are driving up costs. Which change most directly reduces data transfer charges for repeat content?

options.text: Serve the content through Amazon CloudFront to cache at the edge and reduce origin data transfer
Move the instances to a larger type

explanationCorrect: Delivering content via CloudFront caches it at edge locations, so repeat requests are served from the CDN, reducing data transferred out from the origin and often lowering overall transfer cost.
explanationIncorrect: A larger instance type increases compute cost without reducing data transfer. A bigger EBS volume adds storage cost, not transfer savings. Multi-AZ on the database improves availability but does not cut internet egress, so CloudFront caching is the direct cost reducer.

stem: To make a stateless web tier resilient to the loss of a single Availability Zone, what should you do?

options.text: Run instances in multiple AZs behind an Elastic Load Balancer with Auto Scaling
Run all instances in one AZ with a larger size
Use a single instance with frequent reboots
Store sessions only on local disk

explanationCorrect: Distributing instances across multiple AZs behind a load balancer with Auto Scaling means the loss of one zone leaves healthy capacity serving traffic.
explanationIncorrect: Concentrating instances in one AZ leaves the tier fully exposed to that zone's failure. A single instance is a single point of failure regardless of reboots. Storing sessions on local disk ties users to one instance and breaks resilience, so multi-AZ behind an ELB with Auto Scaling is correct.

stem: A relational database must survive an Availability Zone failure with minimal manual effort. Which configuration fits?

options.text: Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment with automatic failover to a standby
A single-AZ RDS instance with nightly snapshots only
Running the database on one EC2 instance
Storing the database in a single S3 object

explanationCorrect: RDS Multi-AZ maintains a synchronous standby in another zone and fails over automatically, providing resilience with little manual intervention.
explanationIncorrect: A single-AZ instance with nightly snapshots loses data since the last snapshot and requires manual restore. A single EC2-hosted database is a manual, single point of failure. A relational database cannot run as one S3 object, so RDS Multi-AZ is the fitting configuration.

stem: Which storage service provides eleven nines of durability by redundantly storing objects across multiple facilities?
explanationCorrect: Amazon S3 is designed for eleven nines of durability by redundantly storing each object across multiple devices and facilities within a Region.
explanationIncorrect: EC2 instance store is ephemeral and lost when the instance stops. A single EBS volume is durable within one AZ but not designed for that cross-facility level alone. Local NVMe on one host has no cross-facility redundancy, so Amazon S3 provides the described durability.

stem: To decouple a spiky producer from a slower consumer so no requests are lost during bursts, which service helps?

options.text: Amazon SQS as a buffer between the components
A direct synchronous call from producer to consumer
Storing requests in a single log file

explanationCorrect: Amazon SQS buffers messages so a burst from the producer is queued and the consumer processes at its own pace without losing requests.
explanationIncorrect: A direct synchronous call couples the two and can drop or block requests during bursts. A single log file is not a managed, scalable queue and risks contention. CloudFront caches content and does not buffer work items, so Amazon SQS is the decoupling buffer.

stem: A workload needs a Region-wide outage recovery strategy with the lowest recovery time and point objectives, at higher cost. Which approach fits?

options.text: A multi-Region active-active or hot standby architecture
Backup and restore to another Region only
A single-Region deployment with no DR
Manual rebuild from documentation after an outage

explanationCorrect: An active-active or hot standby across Regions keeps a running environment ready, minimizing recovery time and data loss at the cost of running duplicate infrastructure.
explanationIncorrect: Backup and restore has the highest recovery time and larger data loss, not the lowest objectives. A single-Region deployment offers no protection against a Region-wide outage. Manual rebuild from documentation is the slowest option, so a multi-Region active-active or hot standby fits the lowest objectives.

stem: Which feature routes users to a healthy endpoint and away from a failed one using health checks and DNS?

options.text: Amazon Route 53 health checks with failover routing

explanationCorrect: Route 53 failover routing uses health checks to direct traffic to a healthy endpoint and away from one that is failing, improving resilience.
explanationIncorrect: S3 versioning preserves object versions and does not route traffic. EBS snapshots back up volumes, not DNS routing. AWS Budgets tracks spending, so Route 53 health checks with failover routing is the correct feature.

stem: To ensure a DynamoDB-backed app survives an AZ failure, what must the architect do about DynamoDB?

options.text: Nothing special, since DynamoDB automatically replicates across multiple AZs in a Region
Manually copy the table to another AZ nightly
Run DynamoDB on a single EC2 instance
Store the table on one EBS volume

explanationCorrect: DynamoDB is a managed service that automatically replicates data across multiple Availability Zones in a Region, so it inherently survives an AZ failure.
explanationIncorrect: Manual nightly copies are unnecessary and risk data loss between copies. DynamoDB is not something you run on your own EC2 instance. It does not sit on a single EBS volume you manage, so relying on its built-in multi-AZ replication is correct.

stem: A fleet behind an ELB occasionally serves errors from unhealthy instances. Which mechanism removes them from rotation automatically?

options.text: Load balancer health checks that stop routing to unhealthy targets

explanationCorrect: ELB health checks continuously test targets and stop sending traffic to any that fail, so unhealthy instances are automatically taken out of rotation.
explanationIncorrect: Increasing instance size does not detect or remove unhealthy instances. Disabling the load balancer removes the very mechanism that routes around failures. Turning off Auto Scaling reduces resilience, so load balancer health checks are the correct mechanism.

stem: Which approach lets an Auto Scaling group replace a failed instance automatically to maintain desired capacity?

options.text: Auto Scaling health checks that terminate and relaunch unhealthy instances
Manually launching a replacement each time

explanationCorrect: Auto Scaling uses health checks to detect unhealthy instances, terminate them, and launch replacements to keep the group at desired capacity.
explanationIncorrect: Manually launching replacements defeats the automation Auto Scaling provides. Ignoring failed instances leaves capacity degraded. Reducing desired capacity to zero removes the workload entirely, so Auto Scaling health checks with automatic replacement is correct.

stem: Which storage option provides shared, elastic file storage accessible from many EC2 instances across AZs?

options.text: A single EBS volume attached to one instance

explanationCorrect: Amazon EFS is an elastic, shared file system that many EC2 instances across Availability Zones can mount concurrently.
explanationIncorrect: A single EBS volume attaches to one instance at a time in one AZ, not shared across many. Instance store is ephemeral local storage. Amazon Glacier is archival, not a live shared file system, so Amazon EFS is the correct shared storage.

stem: To protect against accidental object deletion and enable recovery, which S3 feature should you enable?

options.text: S3 Versioning, optionally with MFA Delete

explanationCorrect: S3 Versioning keeps previous versions of objects so deletions can be undone, and MFA Delete adds protection against unintended or malicious removal.
explanationIncorrect: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads over long distances and does not protect against deletion. Static Website Hosting serves content and offers no recovery. Requester Pays shifts data transfer costs, so S3 Versioning with optional MFA Delete is the correct protection.

stem: Which pattern improves resilience by processing messages so that duplicate deliveries do not cause incorrect results?
explanationCorrect: Idempotent processing ensures that handling the same message more than once yields the same result, which is important because queues may deliver duplicates.
explanationIncorrect: Storing state only in memory risks loss and does not address duplicates. Ignoring all retries can drop legitimate work. Intentionally processing messages twice causes exactly the double-effect idempotency prevents, so idempotent processing is the resilient pattern.

stem: Which service lets you capture and replay changes for point-in-time recovery of a DynamoDB table?
explanationCorrect: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery continuously backs up table data so you can restore to any second within the retention window.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon CloudFront caches content and offers no database recovery. AWS Shield protects against DDoS. Amazon SES sends email, so DynamoDB point-in-time recovery is the correct feature for restoring a table.

stem: To reduce read load on a relational database for frequently accessed data, which service adds an in-memory cache?
explanationCorrect: Amazon ElastiCache provides managed in-memory caching with Redis or Memcached, offloading repeated reads from the database and cutting latency.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon Glacier is archival storage with retrieval delays, the opposite of a fast cache. AWS Snowball transfers data physically. Amazon SES sends email, so Amazon ElastiCache is the in-memory caching service.

stem: A read-heavy relational workload needs to scale reads beyond a single primary instance. Which RDS feature helps?

options.text: Read replicas that serve read traffic

explanationCorrect: RDS read replicas provide additional read-only endpoints, letting you distribute read traffic and scale read capacity horizontally.
explanationIncorrect: The Multi-AZ standby is for failover and does not serve read traffic. Instance store volumes are ephemeral local disks, not a read-scaling feature. S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds S3 uploads, so read replicas are the correct feature for scaling reads.

stem: To serve global users with low latency for static assets, which service caches content near users?
explanationCorrect: Amazon CloudFront caches static assets at edge locations worldwide, reducing latency by serving content close to users.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon RDS is a database, not a content delivery network. AWS Batch runs batch jobs. Amazon Cognito manages authentication, so Amazon CloudFront is the service for low-latency global content delivery.

stem: Which EBS volume type is best suited for a high-throughput big data workload that streams large sequential reads and writes?

options.text: General Purpose SSD for tiny random IO only
Cold HDD for frequent random access

explanationCorrect: Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) is designed for large, sequential throughput-heavy workloads such as big data and log processing.
explanationIncorrect: General Purpose SSD targets a balance of price and performance for smaller random IO, not maximum sequential throughput. Cold HDD is for infrequently accessed data, not frequent access. Instance store is ephemeral and not an EBS type, so Throughput Optimized HDD is the best fit.

stem: An application must handle unpredictable, spiky traffic without managing servers and scale to zero when idle. Which compute choice fits best?

options.text: A fixed fleet of always-on EC2 instances
A Dedicated Host reserved for a year

explanationCorrect: AWS Lambda scales automatically with each event and incurs no charge when idle, fitting spiky, unpredictable traffic without server management.
explanationIncorrect: A fixed always-on fleet pays for idle capacity and requires management. A single large instance cannot scale to zero and is a single point of failure. A year-long Dedicated Host is a costly fixed commitment, so AWS Lambda best fits the requirement.

stem: Which service provides a fully managed, in-memory-accelerated caching layer in front of DynamoDB for microsecond reads?
explanationCorrect: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a managed in-memory cache for DynamoDB that delivers microsecond read latency for eligible requests.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon Athena queries data in S3 with SQL. AWS Glue is an ETL service. Amazon EFS is a shared file system, so DynamoDB Accelerator is the caching layer for DynamoDB.

stem: To improve upload performance for users far from an S3 bucket's Region, which feature helps?
explanationCorrect: S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through nearby edge locations over the optimized AWS network, speeding transfers for distant users.
explanationIncorrect: S3 Versioning retains object versions and does not accelerate transfers. S3 Requester Pays shifts costs to requesters. S3 Object Lock enforces retention, so S3 Transfer Acceleration is the performance feature for distant uploads.

stem: A workload needs to run analytical SQL queries directly on data stored in S3 without loading it into a database first. Which service fits?
explanationCorrect: Amazon Athena runs serverless SQL queries directly against data in S3, with no need to load it into a separate database first.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon RDS requires loading data into a managed relational database. Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, not a query engine over S3. AWS Shield is DDoS protection, so Amazon Athena is the service to query S3 data directly.

stem: Which approach lets a fleet scale out based on a custom application metric such as queue depth?

options.text: Auto Scaling with a target tracking or step policy on a CloudWatch metric
Manually adding instances when someone notices load

explanationCorrect: Auto Scaling can react to CloudWatch metrics like queue depth using target tracking or step scaling policies to add or remove capacity automatically.
explanationIncorrect: Manual scaling when someone notices is slow and error-prone. Disabling metrics removes the signal Auto Scaling needs. A single fixed instance cannot scale at all, so Auto Scaling driven by a CloudWatch metric is the correct approach.

stem: Which purpose-built database is optimized for highly connected data and relationship queries?
explanationCorrect: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database optimized for storing and querying highly connected data and relationships.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon S3 is object storage, not a graph database. Amazon SQS is a message queue. AWS Lambda runs code, so Amazon Neptune is the purpose-built graph database.

stem: A compute-heavy job can be split into many independent tasks. Which design maximizes throughput cost-effectively?

options.text: Parallelize across many instances, using Spot capacity for the interruptible tasks
Run everything sequentially on one instance
Use a single Reserved Instance for a year

explanationCorrect: Splitting the work across many parallel instances increases throughput, and using Spot capacity for interruptible tasks keeps costs low.
explanationIncorrect: Running sequentially on one instance underuses the parallelism available and is slow. A single Reserved Instance still processes serially. Glacier is archival storage and cannot run compute, so parallelizing with Spot capacity maximizes throughput cost-effectively.

stem: Which feature places multiple instances in the same rack-level grouping for the lowest network latency between them?
explanationCorrect: A cluster placement group packs instances close together within an Availability Zone to achieve low latency and high throughput between them.
explanationIncorrect: A security group controls traffic rules, not physical placement. A subnet ACL filters traffic at the subnet level. A launch template defines instance settings but does not group instances for low latency, so a cluster placement group is the correct feature.

stem: Which service streams and processes large volumes of real-time data such as clickstreams?
explanationCorrect: Amazon Kinesis ingests and processes large streams of real-time data like clickstreams and telemetry for immediate analysis.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon Glacier is archival storage, not a streaming service. AWS Artifact provides compliance documents. Amazon Polly synthesizes speech, so Amazon Kinesis is the real-time streaming service.

stem: Which construct controls inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level using stateful rules?
explanationCorrect: A security group acts as a stateful virtual firewall at the instance level, where return traffic is automatically allowed for permitted connections.
explanationIncorrect: A network ACL operates at the subnet level and is stateless, requiring explicit rules for return traffic. An S3 bucket policy governs S3 access, not instance networking. An IAM role grants permissions, not packet filtering, so a security group is the correct instance-level control.

stem: You need private EC2 instances in a private subnet to reach the internet for updates without being reachable from it. What should you use?

options.text: A NAT gateway in a public subnet
An internet gateway attached directly to the private subnet's instances
A public IP on each private instance
A VPC peering connection to the internet

explanationCorrect: A NAT gateway lets instances in a private subnet initiate outbound internet connections for updates while preventing unsolicited inbound connections from the internet.
explanationIncorrect: An internet gateway would make the instances directly reachable, defeating the privacy requirement. Assigning public IPs likewise exposes them inbound. VPC peering connects VPCs, not the public internet, so a NAT gateway is the correct approach.

stem: Which approach grants an application running on EC2 temporary credentials to access S3 securely?

options.text: An IAM role attached to the instance profile

explanationCorrect: An IAM role via the instance profile supplies automatically rotated temporary credentials, avoiding stored long-term keys on the instance.
explanationIncorrect: Hardcoded long-term keys risk leaking durable credentials. Root credentials should never be used by applications given their unrestricted power. A shared password file is insecure and unauditable, so an IAM role on the instance profile is the secure approach.

stem: To let a mobile app access only a specific S3 prefix per user without embedding credentials, which service federates temporary access?

options.text: Amazon Cognito with IAM roles for temporary credentials
Hardcoded keys in the app binary
A public bucket for all users

explanationCorrect: Amazon Cognito federates identities and vends scoped temporary credentials through IAM roles, granting each user access to only their permitted resources.
explanationIncorrect: Hardcoded keys in an app binary can be extracted and abused. A public bucket exposes all users' data to everyone. Emailing credentials is insecure and unscalable, so Amazon Cognito with IAM roles is the correct federation approach.

stem: A database in a private subnet must be reachable only by the application tier, not the internet. Which design enforces this?

options.text: Place the database in a private subnet and allow its security group only from the app tier's security group
Put the database in a public subnet with a public IP

explanationCorrect: Keeping the database in a private subnet and referencing the app tier's security group as the only allowed source restricts access to the application tier alone.
explanationIncorrect: Placing the database in a public subnet with a public IP exposes it to the internet. Opening the port to 0.0.0.0/0 allows the entire internet. Disabling security groups removes protection, so a private subnet with a security-group source restriction enforces the requirement.

stem: Which service stores and rotates database credentials, retrieving them at runtime instead of hardcoding?
explanationCorrect: AWS Secrets Manager securely stores secrets like database credentials, supports automatic rotation, and provides them to applications at runtime.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network. Amazon EFS is a shared file system. AWS Batch runs batch jobs, so AWS Secrets Manager is the service for storing and rotating credentials.

stem: To ensure objects in an S3 bucket are encrypted at rest by default, what should you configure?

options.text: Default bucket encryption using SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS
Public read access on the bucket

explanationCorrect: Enabling default bucket encryption ensures every new object is automatically encrypted at rest with SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS keys.
explanationIncorrect: Public read access exposes data and is unrelated to encryption. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads but does not encrypt at rest. A shorter bucket name has no security effect, so default bucket encryption is the correct configuration.

stem: You want to access S3 from private instances without traversing the public internet or using a NAT gateway. What should you create?

options.text: A public IP on each instance
A Direct Connect to the internet

explanationCorrect: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 routes traffic to S3 privately within the AWS network, avoiding the public internet and NAT charges.
explanationIncorrect: An internet gateway sends traffic over the public internet. Public IPs expose instances and still use the internet path. Direct Connect links your network to AWS, not private instances to S3 within a VPC, so an S3 gateway VPC endpoint is the correct choice.

stem: Which practice enforces separation of duties across many AWS accounts under central governance?

options.text: Using AWS Organizations with service control policies (SCPs)
Giving every user admin in one account

explanationCorrect: AWS Organizations with service control policies centrally governs multiple accounts, setting guardrails that enforce separation and limit permissions across the organization.
explanationIncorrect: Sharing one account for everything prevents separation of duties. Disabling IAM removes access control entirely. Giving every user admin in one account maximizes risk, so AWS Organizations with SCPs is the correct governance practice.

stem: Which service inspects and filters HTTP requests to block SQL injection before they reach your application behind a load balancer?

options.text: AWS WAF associated with the load balancer or CloudFront

explanationCorrect: AWS WAF filters incoming HTTP requests using managed and custom rules to block common attacks like SQL injection when attached to a load balancer or CloudFront.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon Route 53 is DNS and does not inspect HTTP payloads. Amazon EBS is block storage. AWS Glue is an ETL service, so AWS WAF is the service for filtering malicious web requests.

stem: To meet a requirement that encryption keys never leave a hardware boundary you control, which service fits?
explanationCorrect: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules that you control, keeping key material within a validated hardware boundary.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon S3 Standard is object storage, not a key custody solution. AWS Budgets tracks spend. Amazon SNS sends notifications, so AWS CloudHSM meets the dedicated hardware key requirement.

stem: Which practice reduces the attack surface of an application's IAM policies?

options.text: Applying least privilege and scoping policies to specific resources and actions
Granting wildcard permissions on all resources
Sharing one role for unrelated services

explanationCorrect: Scoping IAM policies to only the needed actions and resources follows least privilege and minimizes what a compromised identity could do.
explanationIncorrect: Granting wildcard permissions broadens the attack surface. Attaching AdministratorAccess everywhere removes meaningful restrictions. Sharing one role across unrelated services blurs boundaries and over-grants access, so least privilege with scoped policies is the correct practice.

stem: Which S3 storage class is most cost-effective for data accessed rarely but needing millisecond retrieval when required?

options.text: S3 Express One Zone for hot data

explanationCorrect: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access offers lower storage cost for rarely accessed data while still providing millisecond retrieval when it is needed.
explanationIncorrect: S3 Standard costs more per GB and suits frequently accessed data. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is cheapest but has retrieval times of hours, not milliseconds. S3 Express One Zone targets very hot, latency-sensitive data at higher cost, so Standard-Infrequent Access fits rare access with fast retrieval.

stem: A batch workload runs nightly and can restart if interrupted. Which EC2 pricing minimizes cost?

options.text: A three-year all-upfront Reserved Instance running 24/7

explanationCorrect: Because the batch job tolerates interruption and restart, Spot Instances provide the deepest discount and best fit the fault-tolerant, non-urgent schedule.
explanationIncorrect: On-Demand costs far more for interruptible work. Dedicated Hosts are a premium isolation option. A three-year 24/7 Reserved Instance pays for constant capacity a nightly job does not need, so Spot Instances minimize cost here.

stem: Which feature automatically transitions objects to cheaper storage classes based on age to reduce cost?
explanationCorrect: S3 Lifecycle policies automatically move objects to lower-cost classes or expire them as they age, optimizing storage spend without manual work.
explanationIncorrect: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads, not cost tiering. Object Lock enforces retention for compliance. Requester Pays shifts data transfer costs to requesters, so S3 Lifecycle policies are the cost-optimizing feature.

stem: Which option gives flexible discounts across instance families and Regions in exchange for a committed hourly spend?
explanationCorrect: Compute Savings Plans provide discounts in return for a committed hourly spend and apply flexibly across instance families, sizes, and Regions.
explanationIncorrect: On-Demand has no commitment or discount. Spot offers deep but interruptible discounts without the flexible commitment model described. S3 Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage, not compute commitment, so Compute Savings Plans is the correct option.

stem: Objects have unpredictable and changing access patterns, and the team wants automatic cost optimization without performance impact or retrieval fees. Which S3 class fits?

options.text: S3 One Zone-IA for critical data

explanationCorrect: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on usage, optimizing cost for unpredictable patterns without retrieval fees or performance impact.
explanationIncorrect: Glacier Deep Archive has long retrieval times unsuitable for unpredictable immediate access. Standard alone does not optimize automatically and costs more for cold data. One Zone-IA stores in a single AZ, reducing durability for critical data, so Intelligent-Tiering fits changing patterns.

stem: To reduce cost of a lightly used relational database that can pause when idle, which option helps?

options.text: Amazon Aurora Serverless that scales capacity and can pause when idle
A fleet of On-Demand EC2 databases

explanationCorrect: Aurora Serverless automatically scales database capacity to demand and can pause during idle periods, cutting cost for intermittent workloads.
explanationIncorrect: A large always-on provisioned instance pays for idle capacity. A fleet of self-managed EC2 databases adds operational cost and complexity. Glacier is archival storage and cannot run a live database, so Aurora Serverless best reduces cost for a lightly used database.

stem: Which practice helps identify idle or oversized resources to reduce ongoing spend?

options.text: Right-sizing using AWS Cost Explorer and Compute Optimizer recommendations
Always choosing the largest instance available

explanationCorrect: Right-sizing with Cost Explorer and Compute Optimizer highlights underused or oversized resources so you can downsize and cut spend.
explanationIncorrect: Always choosing the largest instance guarantees waste. Never reviewing utilization leaves overspending undetected. Disabling monitoring removes the data needed to optimize, so right-sizing with these tools is the cost-reducing practice.

stem: A serverless architecture using Lambda and API Gateway had a sudden cost spike. Which factor most likely drove it?

options.text: A surge in request volume, since these services bill per request and execution
The number of IAM users created
The length of the function name
The color of the console theme

explanationCorrect: Lambda and API Gateway are billed by requests and execution, so a surge in traffic directly increases cost, making request volume the likely driver.
explanationIncorrect: The number of IAM users does not drive Lambda or API Gateway usage charges. The function name length has no billing impact. The console theme color is purely cosmetic, so a surge in request volume is the most likely cause.

stem: To avoid paying for a NAT gateway when private instances only need to reach S3 and DynamoDB, what can you use instead?

options.text: Gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB
An internet gateway for each subnet

explanationCorrect: Gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB provide private access at no per-GB endpoint charge, avoiding NAT gateway data processing costs for that traffic.
explanationIncorrect: Adding a second NAT gateway increases cost rather than avoiding it. Public IPs expose instances and still route over the internet. An internet gateway per subnet also uses the public path, so gateway VPC endpoints are the cost-saving alternative.

stem: Which S3 storage class offers the lowest storage cost for long-term archives that tolerate retrieval times of hours?
explanationCorrect: S3 Glacier Deep Archive provides the lowest storage price for long-term data that is rarely accessed and can tolerate multi-hour retrieval.
explanationIncorrect: S3 Standard is priced for frequent access and costs much more per GB. Standard-Infrequent Access is cheaper than Standard but pricier than Deep Archive. The Intelligent-Tiering frequent tier is not the lowest-cost archive option, so Glacier Deep Archive is correct.

stem: A predictable production workload runs steadily 24/7 for years. Which pricing minimizes its compute cost?

options.text: Reserved Instances or a Savings Plan committed for one or three years
Spot Instances for the always-on tier
Recreating instances hourly to reset billing

explanationCorrect: A steady, long-running workload benefits most from a one- or three-year Reserved Instance or Savings Plan commitment, which deeply discounts predictable usage.
explanationIncorrect: On-Demand for years pays full price for predictable capacity. Spot is unsuitable for an always-on production tier that cannot tolerate interruption. Recreating instances hourly does not reset or reduce billing, so a committed Reserved Instance or Savings Plan minimizes cost.

stem: Which approach reduces data transfer costs for serving the same content to many users repeatedly?

options.text: Serving through Amazon CloudFront to cache content at the edge
Serving every request directly from the origin in another Region
Duplicating the origin in every AZ manually

explanationCorrect: CloudFront caches content at edge locations so repeated requests are served from the cache, reducing origin data transfer and often lowering cost.
explanationIncorrect: Serving every request from a distant origin maximizes transfer cost and latency. Disabling caching forces every request back to the origin. Manually duplicating the origin in every AZ adds cost and complexity, so serving through CloudFront reduces repeated transfer costs.
